headline: Haena State Park Reservations and Kalalau Permits
reservation: Access to the Na Pali Coast via Haena State Park requires advanced reservations for parking or the North Shore Shuttle, typically opening 30 days out. These are distinct from Kalalau Trail wilderness camping permits, which are mandatory for hiking beyond Hanakapiai Valley. Changing systems require checking the official Hawaii Department of Land and Natural Resources portal.

days.title: North Shore Coastal Hiking
days.start: Suggested: 7 AM from Hanalei via Shuttle

stops.name: Kee Beach
stops.detail: Begin at the trailhead for the Kalalau Trail, observing the dramatic start of the coastal cliffs.

stops.name: Hanakapiai Beach
stops.detail: Hike the first two miles to see the valley outlet; stay clear of the water due to extreme currents.

days.driving: Allow 45-60 minutes for shuttle transit; road conditions vary near Hanalei.
days.note: Entry requires pre-paid reservations; do not attempt to drive to the trailhead without a parking permit.

days.title: Na Pali from the Ocean
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from Port Allen Harbor

stops.name: Na Pali Cliffs
stops.detail: View the 4,000-foot cathedrals and hanging waterfalls from a licensed boat tour.

stops.name: Nualolo Kai
stops.detail: A historic reef area visible from the water; some tours offer snorkeling depending on sea conditions.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour from South Shore bases; Port Allen is the primary departure point.
days.note: Winter swells often cancel North Shore departures; South Shore trips are more consistent year-round.

days.title: Canyon Overlooks and High Ridges

stops.name: Kalalau Lookout
stops.detail: View the famous emerald valley from 4,000 feet up in Kokee State Park without a strenuous hike.

stops.name: Puu O Kila Lookout
stops.detail: The end of the road offers expansive views of the Alakai Swamp and the coast below.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 to 2 hours for the winding climb from Waimea; conditions vary with rain.
days.note: Clouds often roll in by mid-day; early morning visits offer the best chance for clear valley views.

intel.title: Haena and Kokee Lots
intel.text: Haena parking is strictly limited to permit holders and fills daily; use the official shuttle from Hanalei or Princeville. Kokee State Park lots are larger but can be muddy and crowded during peak summer weekends.

intel.title: Remote Communication
intel.text: Cell service is non-existent on the Kalalau Trail and very spotty in the Kokee highlands. Download all offline maps and reservation QR codes before leaving Hanalei or Waimea.

intel.title: Gateway Fueling
intel.text: Hanalei and Waimea are the final locations for fuel before heading toward the coast or the canyon. There are no gas stations within the State Parks; check levels before the ascent.

intel.title: Ocean Conditions
intel.text: May through September typically offers calmer seas for boat tours and kayaking. Winter months bring massive North Shore surf that makes water access dangerous and often leads to trip cancellations.

intel.title: Stream Crossings
intel.text: The Kalalau Trail involves crossing Hanakapiai Stream; flash flooding can make this impassable instantly. Never cross a rising stream and check the weather forecast for the upper mountains, not just the beach.

plan.arrival: Fly into Lihue (LIH), pick up a rental car, and stock up on supplies in Lihue or Kapaa. Most North Shore bases are a 60-90 minute drive from the airport.
plan.vehicle: A standard vehicle is fine for paved roads, but check rental contracts for restrictions on Kokee dirt roads; RVs are not recommended for the narrow, winding Highway 560.
plan.goldenHour: Kalalau Lookout at sunset provides a dramatic interplay of light and shadow on the ridges; bring a jacket for the high elevation.
